section_summary: The section concludes a lengthy report on Japan’s 1949 deflation, examining industrial stockpiles, subsidies, unemployment, wages, household spending and farm finances before recommending investment in basic industries. It then contains airgrams on trade controls, labour and foreign commerce, followed by a despatch and information bulletin on American aid to Japan. The final pages begin a separate despatch summarising an October economic report.

subfiles.title: Report on deflationary trends in the Japanese economy
subfiles.about: Assesses the industrial and social effects of Japan’s 1949 deflation and proposes investment to support recovery.
subfiles.summary: The report surveys difficulties in coal, power, metals, chemicals, transport equipment, textiles and other industries, especially falling demand, unpaid accounts and growing stockpiles. It examines subsidies, Kodan financing, distribution controls, unemployment, wages, small businesses, urban living standards and farm finances. Its conclusion attributes deflation partly to reduced public investment, suspended Reconstruction Finance Bank lending, delayed counterpart funding and weak exports; it urges carefully timed government investment in basic infrastructure. The closing pages contain economic charts.

subfiles.title: Airgram on possible revival of export associations
subfiles.from: U.S. Political Adviser for Japan, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Reports discussions of legislation and administrative arrangements for Japanese export associations.
subfiles.summary: The airgram describes plans for export associations to address foreign exchange, export prices and quality, and notes discussion of whether Trade Association Law amendments should be introduced through the Diet.

subfiles.title: Cover note forwarding a letter to the Political Adviser
subfiles.from: Edward E. Doherty, Office of Northeast Asian Affairs
subfiles.to: Acting United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Forwards a copy of John M. Allison’s November 23 letter for SCAP’s information.
subfiles.summary: Forwards Allison’s letter to Robert R. Rest.

subfiles.title: Tokyo airgram A-294 on economic and labour developments
subfiles.from: U.S. Political Adviser for Japan, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Reports observations from Osaka and Kobe and developments in American trade, labour and Japanese foreign commerce.
subfiles.summary: The airgram describes bomb damage and slow rehabilitation in Osaka and Kobe, predicts departures by financially weak American traders, and discusses labour unions, railway wages and declining real income. It also covers dissatisfaction with a German trade arrangement and prospective trade negotiations involving India and Pakistan.

subfiles.title: Tokyo airgram on export association legislation
subfiles.from: U.S. Political Adviser for Japan, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Discusses a draft bill to legalise Japanese export associations and their proposed powers.
subfiles.summary: Calvin Verity discusses a bill that would permit export associations to coordinate prices, quality, quotas, cooperative projects and market information, with exemptions from existing trade and monopoly rules.

subfiles.title: Tokyo airgram A-303 on economic and trade developments
subfiles.from: U.S. Political Adviser for Japan, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Reports several Japanese economic policy and foreign trade matters.
subfiles.summary: The surviving OCR is heavily damaged. Legible passages refer to counterpart funding, economic administration, Dr. Fine’s observations, and trade questions involving Latin America, Mexico and the Netherlands.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 791 transmitting ‘American Aid to Japan’
subfiles.from: Acting U.S. Political Adviser for Japan, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Transmits a GHQ information bulletin on the changing purpose of American aid to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Transmits the bulletin and highlights aid’s shift toward economic balance and payments support.

subfiles.title: Information Bulletin No. 26: American Aid to Japan
subfiles.from: Public Information Office, General Headquarters, Far East Command
subfiles.about: Explains how American aid imports and counterpart funds support Japan’s economy.
subfiles.summary: The bulletin describes a shift from emergency relief toward economic rehabilitation, a balanced economy and balance of payments support. It gives figures for aid financed imports, including food, petroleum products and cotton, and explains the purposes and deposits of the yen counterpart fund. It also notes transfers of surplus material and benefits beyond directly funded imports.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 77 transmitting October monthly economic report
subfiles.from: U.S. Political Adviser for Japan, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Transmits an October 1949 economic report and notes aid, subsidy and production developments.
subfiles.summary: Notes counterpart fund loans, planned subsidy reductions and forthcoming analysis of the Shoup Mission’s recommendations.
